paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Paul says, "Everything is permissible," but not everything is beneficial (1 Corinthians 10:23). Allowed and helpful are two DIFFERENT things. Just because you CAN doesn't mean it's the move.

So what's the question to ask? Paul says, "No one should seek his own good, but the good of others" (1 Corinthians 10:24). The meat market was fine, because "The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof" (1 Corinthians 10:26). But if someone says the food was offered to idols, Paul says to skip it for the sake of the one who told you (1 Corinthians 10:28). Giving up a little freedom for somebody else is not losing, friend. It's love.

And it all gets one finish line: "So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God" (1 Corinthians 10:31). Paul lives it, seeking the good of many "that they may be saved" (1 Corinthians 10:33). Then he says, "You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ" (1 Corinthians 11:1). So follow Jesus, baker, and let your everyday choices point people to Him.
